Hesai launches Kosmo to turn real spaces into robot-training scenes

Kosmo One capture hardware and Kosmo World processing generate 3DGS, mesh and depth assets.

Hesai / PRNewswire ↗14 October 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3

Capturing environments for simulation

Hesai launched Kosmo on October 14. Kosmo One combines LiDAR, a one-inch imaging sensor and an IMU to capture geometry, appearance and camera position. Kosmo World processes the data into scenes for robot training and world models.

Several assets from one reconstruction

The platform generates 3D Gaussian Splatting, mesh and depth data, with object segmentation and AI filling of unscanned areas. It supports Isaac Sim and Isaac Lab. Hesai estimates 15 minutes to scan a typical 100-square-metre room, depending on layout.

Specifications and reported results

Maximum capture is 8K, but exported files top out at 6K. Hesai cites a DQ deployment with 99% Sharpa task success and much faster scene preparation. Those vendor-reported case results are not a general benchmark or guarantee.
